SQL CAN'T BE SKIPPED
If you’re in data — whether as a Data Engineer, Analyst, BI Developer, or even a Software Engineer — you can’t escape SQL.
It’s the universal language to talk to your data.
I recently came across this excellent breakdown of SQL essentials, which covers everything you should know to become confident and effective at data querying and manipulation.
Here’s a quick walkthrough of these topics and why each one matters
✅ 1. Fundamentals of SQL
Get crystal clear on SELECT, FROM, WHERE. This is where everything starts — fetching data from tables.
✅ 2. Filtering Commands
Learn how to use WHERE, IN, BETWEEN, LIKE, and logical operators to filter your data precisely.
✅ 3. Ordering Commands
Sort your results using ORDER BY. Simple but critical when generating reports.
✅ 4. Alias
Use AS to rename columns or tables for readability and cleaner joins.
✅ 5. Aggregate Commands
Functions like SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT — vital for dashboards, summaries, and metrics.
✅ 6. GROUP BY Commands
Break down data into groups to run aggregates on. Mastering GROUP BY + HAVING is a game changer.
✅ 7. Conditional Statements
Use CASE WHEN to build logic inside your queries. It replaces multiple queries with one smart statement.
✅ 8. JOINS
The heart of relational databases. Understand INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN, RIGHT JOIN, FULL OUTER JOIN, and SELF JOIN.
✅ 9. Subquery
Run queries inside queries. Essential for breaking down complex logic.
✅ 10. VIEW & INDEX
VIEW: Save complex queries as virtual tables.
INDEX: Speed up read performance dramatically — learn when and how to create them.
✅ 11. String Functions
CONCAT, SUBSTR, REPLACE, LENGTH help you clean and manipulate text data.
✅ 12. Mathematical Functions
From ROUND to MOD — small tools that make numerical data handling powerful.
✅ 13. Date-Time Functions
Calculate age, format dates, or compare timestamps — critical for almost every business analysis.
✅ 14. Pattern Matching (Regex)
Find complex patterns inside strings. Think of filtering emails, phone numbers, or specific text structures.
✅ 15. Data Type Conversion Functions
CAST and CONVERT are must-haves when your data is not in the type you need.
Pro Tip for Learners:
✅ Practice with public datasets (Kaggle, Google BigQuery, or sample retail databases).
✅ Start simple, then write queries combining JOINS, GROUP BY, subqueries, and window functions.
✅ Use EXPLAIN PLAN to see how your queries execute and optimize them.
